thread:
maria (eng-platform): Quick sync — we're finalizing the private/VPC metrics export contract. Need to nail down: allowed egress patterns, auth model for the agent, KMS audit hooks, and the minimal metrics schema the runtime will emit. Who's got blockers?

ajay (eng-infra): Customers will only allow outbound 443 in most cases. No custom ports. So the agent must speak HTTPS and work behind customer proxies.

tasha (eng-sre): Also need to decide on persistent IPs vs DNS. Many customers whitelist IPs; ephemeral NATs will cause support churn. Can we offer a static egress IP range for Dedicated/private installs?

lucas (runtime): For agent side, we can do HTTPS to a customer endpoint and multiplex metrics and audit logs over an HTTP/2 stream. That keeps only port 443 needed. We can also do mutual TLS if they require client certs.

ken (security): mTLS is preferred for high-sensitivity customers. However, some on-prem envs prefer JWT-based service-to-service tokens managed by their IdP. We should support both: mTLS (certs) + fallback to signed JWT with KMS-backed validation.

maria (eng-platform): Good. For KMS hooks: we need to push a copy of export events (audit trails) to customer KMS-encrypted blob storage and also emit an audit-line to their SIEM via syslog/HTTPS. Does that match legal/compliance asks?

ken (security): Yes, but two notes: (1) we cannot hold plaintext keys. Agent must encrypt payload client-side with their KMS key (customer-provided CMK ARN/URL). (2) We need integrated signing for our control-plane->agent handshake so we can rotate CA without breaking customers.

ajay (eng-infra): Implementation constraints: the agent runs inside customer VPC. It can make outbound connections only. We'll need a small bootstrap handshake over HTTPS to exchange agent_id <-> signed_challenge. Example sequence:

```
# bootstrap (agent -> control-plane)
POST https://cp.redwood-infra.example/v1/agent/register
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <signed-jwt-from-customer>
Body: { "agent_id": "uuid", "sni": "customer.example" }
# cp responds with agent config + cert options, and allowed endpoints for metrics export
```

lucas (runtime): For metrics payload, we propose a compact schema to reduce churn: one line JSON per record, newline-delimited. Fields: ts, model, route, p50_ms, p95_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_hit_ratio, host_id. Sample: `{"ts":1680000000,"model":"rw-70b","p50_ms":23,...}`

maria (eng-platform): We'll need a mapping from those runtime fields to console dashboards. Ideally the agent will label metrics with canonical route IDs and model variant to support rollouts and canary comparisons.

tasha (eng-sre): Also add a heartbeat metric and a signed sequence number to detect reorder/dup. We need that for alerting when exports stop.

ken (security): Audit hooks: every exported file should be accompanied by a minimal audit-envelope signed with the customer's KMS key or our HSM-provided delegations. We should support customer-requested hash verification endpoints.

ajay (eng-infra): Networking doc items for customers:
- outbound: 443 only
- SNI must match provided endpoint
- allow TLSv1.2+ and modern ciphers
- optional mTLS where both sides present certs

maria (eng-platform): Who owns the dashboard mapping? Platform will own the console surfaces, but runtime teams must guarantee stable field names and types. We need a small contract YAML that runtime emits and platform consumes. Draft: `metrics-contract-v1.yaml` with fields + semantics.

lucas (runtime): We can generate that contract from the runtime build. Will add tests to ensure schema compatibility. Also plan to include a per-route sample load distribution so Optimize can suggest batching thresholds.

maria (eng-platform): Ops question — when agent can't reach customer endpoint (e.g., customer firewall), do we buffer locally and retry, or fallback to pushing to an intermediate Redwood relay (with customer consent)?

tasha (eng-sre): Buffering is fine short-term, but we need bounded disk usage and a hard SLA on buffering time (e.g., 48h). Relay should be opt-in only — some customers won't allow it. Any relay must be end-to-end encrypted with customer KMS.

ken (security): Relay requires explicit contractual approval. Also need key escrow rules and key provenance logs for audits.

maria (eng-platform): Action items: 
- ajay: write the customer network checklist doc (egress IP options, proxy env, SNI rules) — due EOD Fri.
- lucas: produce metrics-contract-v1.yaml and sample payloads + test harness — due Tue.
- tasha: define heartbeat + buffer policy and alerting thresholds for Console — due Mon.
- ken: write KMS/encryption guidance + audit-envelope format and rotation plan — due Tue.

ajay (eng-infra): I'll also prototype a small NAT/static-egress blueprint for our private appliance offering.

lucas (runtime): I'll add sequence numbers and kv_cache_hit_ratio to the schema.

maria (eng-platform): Great — once we have those, Platform will wire up dashboard templates (route comparisons, canary vs baseline) and a per-customer export health panel.

deploy-bot: deploy event: metrics-export-proto v0.1 pushed to staging (build 202).

maria (eng-platform): Awesome. If anyone hits blockers during implementation ping #eng-platform and DM me. We'll schedule a 30m cross-team call next week to review the first end-to-end run. :calendar:
